text: A goal-directed query that knows an argument a rule's head computes by asking a question of its own, such as `["query", ["meant", {"revenue": "t"}, "?q"]]` over `["rule", ["base", "?q", ["array/reduce", ["find", "?key", ["reading", "?key"]], "?q", ["lambda", ["rest", "key"], ["object/remove", "rest", "key"]]]], ["answer", "?q", "?_"]]` and `["rule", ["meant", "?base", "?q"], ["base", "?q", "?base"]]`, gives the answers of full evaluation again, instead of failing with an internal error, `undefined is not an object (evaluating 'literal.parts')`. The rewrite took the `find`'s own `?key` for a variable the rule had to bind first. This is the `meant` relation of the lion-research skill. The rewrite now follows the asking rule wherever it asks what a value needs: a query whose argument is computed by a question with variables of its own, such as `["path", ["array/reduce", ["find", "?a", ["start", "?a"]], 0, ["lambda", ["sum", "a"], ["number/add", "sum", "a"]]], "?to"]`, now derives only what it reaches, as one that writes the value does.
